notes: Example answers offered as buttons on the LAST introduction question, the one that asks what kind of solution the visitor is looking at. Chosen by their department, falling back to their role. Read by app/src/interestExamples.ts, and copied into the OAT_DIGITAL_ROOM_store_visitor_profile Code node in Cognigy, which has no HTTP fetch in front of it and so cannot read this file.
why: That question asks a stranger to compose a sentence about what they want, which is the hardest question in the introduction and the one most likely to produce a shrug. An example they can tap costs them nothing and gives retrieval something specific to work with. The visitor can still ignore all of them and type whatever they like: these are examples, not a menu.
guarantee: EVERY value here must return at least one asset from the catalog. tools/test-interest-examples.mjs asserts that against the real searchCatalog and fails the build otherwise, which is what protects the live agent. The portal additionally filters at runtime, so an example that stopped matching would simply not be offered. An example button that leads nowhere is worse than no button.
notAssetTitles: These are PHRASINGS, not asset names. Offering three asset titles here would narrow the visitor to our content before we know what they came for, and it would make the interest field a title rather than their goal. find_demo offers titles later, once there is an intent to search on.
